nodes.description: Serum interleukin 7 normally rises in inverse proportion to the circulating CD4 count and drives regeneration of the compartment. In these patients that relationship is much weaker than in other causes of CD4 depletion, so the loop that should refill the compartment does not respond to its emptying. Recorded as provisional: the observation is a correlation between a serum cytokine level and a cell count, and the step that fails between them has not been identified.

nodes.description: About a third of patients carry an autoimmune condition, and 44 autoimmune diagnoses were made in 33 of the 91 patients in the largest cohort. nodes.description: The defining lesion and the one step every case shares: a circulating CD4 T cell count persistently below 300 cells per cubic millimetre, confirmed on separate occasions, with no infectious, iatrogenic or monogenic cause found. The median count in the largest cohort was 80 cells per cubic millimetre. CD8 counts are reduced alongside CD4 in about half of patients, and natural killer and B cell numbers less often, so the depletion is frequently not confined to the CD4 lineage. Counts drift upward slightly over years rather than falling, which is what separates the natural history from untreated HIV infection.

nodes.description: The only intervention tested prospectively against the depletion itself. An open-label phase 1/2A dose-escalation trial of recombinant human interleukin 7 raised circulating CD4 and CD8 counts and tissue-resident T cells in gut mucosa and bone marrow, and the cells produced cytokines on stimulation. Injection-site reactions were the commonest adverse event; one patient made non-neutralising anti-interleukin-7 antibodies, and one developed systemic lupus erythematosus on study. A long-acting form, efineptakin alfa, is in a phase 1/2 trial, and one patient in the NIH cohort was receiving it for refractory papillomavirus disease.
